issue.title: Mobile Menu Background Transparency Issue
issue.description: The mobile navigation menu panel appears transparent despite multiple attempts to apply a solid background color. The background content is visible through the menu panel.
issue.affected_element: Mobile menu panel (motion.div with className 'fixed right-0 top-0 bottom-0 w-80')

symptoms: Mobile menu panel background appears transparent/semi-transparent
Background content (blurred images, text) visible through menu panel
Computed styles show correct values but visual rendering is still transparent
Backdrop blur effect may be interfering with background opacity
root_cause_hypothesis: Framer Motion animation variants controlling opacity may be overriding inline styles
CSS specificity conflicts between Tailwind classes and inline styles
Backdrop blur filter creating visual transparency effect even with solid background
Browser rendering issue with backdrop-filter and background-color combination
Possible CSS cascade issue where parent elements or global styles are affecting opacity

attempted_fixes.description: Removed bg-black/40 and changed to bg-gray-900
Removed backdrop-blur-md and added inline styles
changes: Added inline style with backgroundColor: '#111827', opacity: 1, backdropFilter: 'none'
Removed opacity from menuVariants (only animate x position)
Kept inline styles with solid background

attempted_fixes.description: Used ref callback to apply styles with !important
changes: Added ref callback using el.style.setProperty() with 'important' flag
attempted_fixes.result: Partially successful - computed styles show correct values but visual rendering still appears transparent

attempted_fixes.description: Added setTimeout in ref callback to ensure styles apply after Framer Motion
changes: Attempted to apply styles after Framer Motion animation completes

current_code.className: fixed right-0 top-0 bottom-0 w-80 z-50 lg:hidden shadow-xl
current_code.ref_callback: Uses setTimeout to apply styles with !important flags via setProperty

visual_rendering.description: Despite computed styles showing correct values, the menu panel visually appears transparent with background content visible through it

backdrop_element.status: Working correctly - provides dark backdrop behind menu

potential_solutions.description: Use CSS module or global CSS with !important
potential_solutions.approach: Create a CSS module or add global CSS rule targeting the menu panel with !important flags
potential_solutions.rationale: CSS specificity might be higher than inline styles in some cases

potential_solutions.description: Remove Framer Motion opacity animation completely
potential_solutions.approach: Only animate transform (x position), never animate opacity. Set opacity to 1 in all states.
potential_solutions.rationale: Framer Motion might be creating a stacking context or rendering layer that affects opacity

potential_solutions.description: Use a wrapper div with solid background
potential_solutions.approach: Wrap the menu content in an inner div with solid background, keep outer div for animation
potential_solutions.rationale: Separate animation container from background container

potential_solutions.description: Check for parent element opacity or transform
potential_solutions.approach: Inspect parent elements in the DOM for any opacity or transform properties that might create a stacking context
potential_solutions.rationale: Parent elements with opacity < 1 or transforms create new stacking contexts

potential_solutions.approach: Set CSS variables in inline styles and use them in a style tag
potential_solutions.rationale: CSS variables might have different specificity behavior

potential_solutions.approach: Check if any parent elements have backdrop-filter that might be affecting rendering
potential_solutions.rationale: Backdrop filters can create rendering layers that affect child elements

potential_solutions.approach: Use ::before pseudo-element with absolute positioning and solid background
potential_solutions.rationale: Pseudo-elements can sometimes bypass certain rendering issues

debugging_information.notes: This appears to be a browser rendering/compositing issue where computed styles are correct but visual rendering doesn't match. This can happen with backdrop-filter, transform, or opacity animations creating new rendering layers.

recommendations: Try Solution 2 first (remove opacity from Framer Motion variants)
If that fails, try Solution 3 (wrapper div approach)
Check browser DevTools Layers panel to see if multiple rendering layers are being created
Test in different browsers to see if issue is browser-specific
Consider using CSS-in-JS solution (styled-components, emotion) for more control over specificity
Check if there are any global CSS rules affecting fixed positioned elements
